questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important that students had a lot of hands-on and patient flow was sufficient.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a great experience, I wish it would have lasted longer. However, be prepared that the teaching is both in Finnish and English. Teachers would talk to exchange students in English however, would change to Finnish when addressing the Finnish students.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: All information were provided through email exchange and newsletters.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The first day was an introduction day, where we were introduced to the hospital facilities, got our keys, badges and met with our mentors.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Everything was great and well-organized.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: After having problems with the apartment received from HOAS, I managed to find housing through Unihome. It was more expensive but worth every penny.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It took me around an hour to travel every day. However, there are Unihome student apartments close by Viikki campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Hoas apartments for students were not good. I was satisfied with Unihome, however, price was substantially higher.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All registration was made by our coordinator.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Everything went online through mobility and email exchange.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Erasmus coordinator was a great help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I were registered for all the wanted classes. I wrote in the beginning to our coordinator that I would like to have small animal focus, and I got 13 weeks at the Small Animal Hospital. It was great.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write to the Erasmus coordinator, and ask for your preferred rotations. Most of the time they could accommodate my wishes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I spent 13 weeks at the Small Animal Hospital rotating through different departments.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The rotations are week-based. The students at the host institution are stronger in the practical aspects, they, however I felt I had a better theoretical knowledge. In the end it was great, because I got a lot of hands-on experience and learned quite a few different procedures, that I would have not had a chance to do at UCPH. In addition I had an exotic day, where I had different kind of exotic patients (reptiles, birds, rodents).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Anesthesia, small animal general policlinics, diagnostic imaging, neurology – ophthalmology - dentistry, small animal on-call duty, small animal internal medicine ward, small animal dermatology – cardiology - exotics, small animal surgery policlinics, small animal surgery operating theatre

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All the small animal courses listed above. They were great and I have learned a lot. Teachers are also very nice and helpful.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: They have a great canteen. A big lunch meal with coffee cost around 4 euro.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation. However, if you live close to the campus, you can walk or bike there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were not much planned non-academic opportunities for exchange students. However, the group of exchange students self-organized events and outings.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sitsit is a kind of student party organized by the Finnish student association.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sitsit

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Nuksio national park

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Finnish people are shy. Don't be afraid to ask and talk to them, eventually they will open up.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Norms

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't be afraid to ask, even if the conversation is going on in Finnish. 
Prepare for the next day patients and use translate for journals.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use your time wisely, 3 months goes by really fast.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Academic components and being in Helsinki.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Some students and vets would forget to speak in English.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I would recommend this exchange program to anyone who would like to improve their practical skills.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
